clue.text: Perfect place associated primarily with high-class headgear

parts.note: U is the old abbreviation for upper-class, as in U and non-U
a topi is a sun helmet, a pith hat

indicators.note: primarily asks for only the leading letter of the word associated

explanation.surface: An ideal spot linked mainly with posh hats.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the pieces out of order: 'associated primarily' gives the final A, after U and TOPI.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More's imagined island has become the standard word for an ideal society or perfect place.

clue.text: Girl who covers old doctor with trifle?

indicators.note: covers says the trifle wraps around the old doctor, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, something of little value
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A girl who conceals an elderly medic with a pudding, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Trifle suggests the British custard-and-sponge pudding; here it means a plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomboy is a girl who enjoys rough, boyish activities, so the definition names her generally.

clue.text: Soldier claimed to be organised like ambulance crews …

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: organised means the letters of claimed are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier insists he was arranged in the manner of ambulance staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramedical describes support medical work such as that done by ambulance crews and paramedics.

clue.text: … he's invested in suitable American equipment

indicators.note: invested in means placed within, as one is invested in an office, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: apt means suitable
he refers back to the soldier of the previous clue, a para

explanation.surface: Continuing the soldier story: he puts money into fitting US gear.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 3 Down: 'he' is that clue's soldier, and 'invested in' puts him inside the word for suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is a general word for equipment or a set of instruments for a task.

clue.text: Soft drink the French imbibed with salad

indicators.note: imbibed means taken in, so the French article goes inside the drink

parts.note: cola is a soft drink
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Someone had a fizzy drink with their salad, like the French do.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage, usually dressed with mayonnaise.

clue.text: What we may say, seeing attractive moulding?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise or admiration
nice means attractive or pleasant

explanation.surface: Our exclamation on seeing an attractive piece of plasterwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the clue as 'Cor, nice!', the remark someone makes on seeing something attractive; 'cor' is British slang for wow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornice is an ornamental moulding running round a wall just below the ceiling.

clue.text: Authorised learner knocked over most of drink

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate letter

indicators.note: knocked over means tipped upside down, so in a down clue the letters are read backwards
most of means the last letter of the drink is dropped

parts.note: lager is a drink, a light beer

explanation.surface: An approved learner driver spills nearly all their pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the drink's last letter, and 'knocked over' turns the remainder upside down, as a down clue allows; the learner's letter goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legal is permitted by law, so it is authorised.

clue.text: Go astray over in Ascension Island

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the letters are turned upside down, read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the words Ascension Island

explanation.surface: Wandering off course while over on a remote Atlantic island.
explanation.walkthrough: The run NIS spans ascensioN ISland; 'over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To sin is to stray morally, to go astray from the right path.

clue.text: Creature's way, in Bible, to board a rescue vessel

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition reads 'Creature is'

indicators.note: to board means to go aboard, so the inner pieces get inside a + ark

parts.note: Noah's ark was the vessel that rescued the animals from the flood

indicators.note: in places the road inside the Bible abbreviation

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
RD, road, is a way

explanation.surface: An animal's path, as told in scripture, leads it on board Noah's boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: 'in' puts the road inside the Bible version, and 'to board' puts that inside a + the rescue vessel, Noah's boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark is a burrowing African mammal, a creature that eats ants and termites.

clue.text: Inappropriate comment of rugby player meeting queen

parts.note: a forward in the front row of the scrum might say 'I'm prop'
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A rude remark by a rugby forward on meeting the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A prop is a front-row forward in rugby; his comment 'I'm prop' runs into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Improper and inappropriate are synonyms, both meaning unsuitable or unseemly.

clue.text: Good record people of breeding show

parts.note: an entry is a record, an item written in a register

explanation.surface: A fine pedigree list shows the aristocracy.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are well-born people ranking just below the nobility, people of good breeding.

clue.text: Jolly active person seen outside window

indicators.note: seen outside means the active person surrounds the other piece

parts.note: a doer is an active person
a jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A cheerful energetic person spotted outside a window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' looks like an adjective, but it is navy slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormer is a window set in a sloping roof, projecting vertically from it.

clue.text: Maltreatment received I see as unreal

indicators.note: received means taken in, so the I and see go inside maltreatment

parts.note: ill use is maltreatment
V, vide, is Latin for see in references

explanation.surface: Someone sees their abuse as not real.
explanation.definitionFit: Illusive means deceptive, based on illusion, so not real.

clue.text: Sensational act reveals leading agent's set-up

parts.note: shows means reveals
top means leading, foremost

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a rep, a sales representative, is an agent; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A star turn exposes how the main agent's organisation works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' turns REP into PER at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A showstopper is a performance so impressive that applause halts the show, a sensational act.

clue.text: Serve as host at a royal investiture, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: to act as host, pouring the drinks or carving the meat
literally, what a monarch does there: conferring titles and awards

explanation.surface: Acting as host at the palace ceremony where medals are given out.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to perform a host's duties, and literally describes conferring honours at an investiture.

clue.text: In Poole he represented a port authority

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man from Poole stood in for an official running the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Poole is a harbour town in Dorset, so 'port authority' looks like a harbour board; it is an expert on port wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An oenophile is a wine lover and connoisseur, so an authority on port.

clue.text: Shoot attendant for failure to reach target

parts.note: a slip is a cutting or young shoot taken from a plant
a page is a young attendant

explanation.surface: Fire the assistant for missing goals.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippage is the amount by which a project falls short of its target or schedule.

clue.text: Aussie town band welcomed by Miss Liddell's private secretary

parts.note: Alice Liddell was the girl who inspired Alice in Wonderland

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken in by the following piece, so the band goes inside

parts.note: PS is the abbreviation for private secretary
a ring is a band

explanation.surface: A town's musicians are greeted by the aide of Lewis Carroll's young muse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but it is a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice Springs is a town in the Northern Territory in central Australia.

clue.text: Proper clothing has no black pigment

parts.note: real means proper, genuine

indicators.note: has no means a letter is removed from the clothing

parts.note: garb is clothing
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Respectable dress contains no dark colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Realgar is an orange-red arsenic sulphide mineral once used as a pigment.

clue.text: Smooth top of table, one of seven in suite

parts.note: to plane wood is to smooth it

indicators.note: top of in a down clue asks for the first letter of the word table

explanation.surface: Level the surface of a table, one of a set of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suite' suggests furniture; it is Holst's orchestral suite The Planets, which has seven movements.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the seven movements of Holst's The Planets suite is named after a planet.

clue.text: Wood by a river incorporating initially a form of defence

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the wood beside the a river pieces

parts.note: the Po is the main river of northern Italy
a log is a piece of wood

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letters of incorporating and a

explanation.surface: A timber beside a river takes in a defensive structure.
explanation.walkthrough: The text held read 'mutually' for 'initially', an OCR slip. 'incorporating' looks like a container signal, but it gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence of one's opinions or conduct.

clue.text: Zest a theatre cat reduced excessively

parts.note: Gus is the Theatre Cat in T S Eliot's Old Possum poems and the musical Cats

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: too means excessively

explanation.surface: Liveliness of a stage cat cut down far too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto means enthusiasm and enjoyment, the same as zest.

clue.text: Lackey old duke included in staff

indicators.note: included in means placed inside the staff

parts.note: a pole is a staff

explanation.surface: An aged noble's servant is among the household staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees; it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle, figuratively, is a servile follower, a lackey who does another's bidding.

clue.text: Undermine plan to return to part of South America

indicators.note: to return means go back, so the two words together are read backwards

parts.note: to sap is to undermine
a map is a plan

explanation.surface: Sabotage a scheme to go back to a region of the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses SAPMAP as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast grassy plains of Argentina and neighbouring countries.

clue.text: Old man consuming Oriental food item

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so the father takes the other letter inside

parts.note: pa is a father, one's old man
E, east, stands for Oriental

explanation.surface: Dad eating something from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: A pea is a small green seed eaten as a vegetable, an item of food.

clue.text: Sensational as one's vices may be

definitions.meaning: a vice is a clamp, and clamps are holding tight

explanation.definitionFit: The word means enthralling, and also describes a vice clamping hold of something.

clue.text: Attack or support the political Left

definitions.meaning: to beat or assail verbally at length
read as two words, to back Britain's left-wing party

explanation.surface: A choice between attacking or backing the left.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is Britain's main left-of-centre party; 'be Labour' is to support it.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour is to attack, physically or with words, and split it means to be a Labour supporter.

clue.text: Returning in time, Jack corrected mistakes

indicators.note: in places the turned sailor inside the time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the sailor's word is read backwards

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, a tar

explanation.surface: Coming back just in time, a sailor fixed errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name but is a sailor; 'Returning' turns him round and 'in' places him inside the period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed errors in a book, published with their corrections.
